# Skill: nature-literature-pipeline

# Nature Literature Pipeline

A complete, production-tested automated literature pipeline. Not just "search for papers" — it's a structured engine that scores, classifies, reads, delivers, and archives research papers daily.

## What It Does

```
Cron (daily trigger, e.g. 08:30)
  │
  ├─ ① SEARCH (30 candidates)
  │   arXiv / OpenAlex / Crossref / Semantic Scholar (auto-degradation)
  │
  ├─ ② COARSE FILTER (30 → 5)
  │   Six-dimension scoring: topic match × 35 + methodology × 20
  │   + journal quality × 15 + network relevance × 10
  │   + applied value × 10 + archival value × 10
  │
  ├─ ③ FINE READ (top 5)
  │   Abstract-level or full-text. Source level tagged:
  │   Full-text / Abstract only / Metadata only
  │
  ├─ ④ DELIVER
  │   Formatted digest to Feishu/Telegram/etc.
  │   🏅 rank | title | journal | ⭐ score | 💡 one-liner
  │   🔬 methods | 📊 key results | 🧭 commentary
  │
  └─ ⑤ ARCHIVE
      DOI/arXiv de-dup → classify → write notes → update index
```

## Quick Start

After installing, tell your agent:

```
My research area is [X], keywords: [Y], deliver to [feishu group name], archive to [path]
```

The agent will configure keywords, delivery target, and archive path automatically.

Then set up a daily cron job:

```
Set up a daily literature push at 08:30 Beijing time, 30 candidates, top 5 delivered
```

## Architecture

The skill is organized in two layers:

| Layer | Purpose | Files |
|-------|---------|-------|
| **Engine** | Scoring, classification, note templates, gap analysis | `references/scoring-system.md`, `references/gap-analysis.md`, `references/note-template.md` |
| **Application** | Daily cron pipeline, delivery formatting, archival workflow | `references/push-format.md`, `references/cron-setup.md`, `references/review-compilation-workflow.md` |

## Configuration

All domain-specific content is configurable:

- **Keywords** — your research keywords (English + Chinese)
- **Scoring weights** — adjust the six dimensions for your field
- **Classification rules** — define your own tier system (A-E or custom)
- **Delivery target** — Feishu group, Telegram channel, email, etc.
- **Archive path** — local vault/wiki directory

A config template is provided in `templates/literature-push-template.md`.

## Built-in Safeguards

- **Score validation**: Each dimension capped, total recalculated — no 11/10 allowed
- **Triple de-duplication**: DOI / arXiv ID / OpenAlex ID
- **Graceful degradation**: Semantic Scholar down → auto-switch to OpenAlex + Crossref + arXiv
- **Read-only archive**: Daily pipeline writes to `raw/` literature directory only; never modifies wiki/knowledge base without user approval

## Related Skills

- `nature-academic-search` — ad-hoc literature search (complementary; this skill adds structured daily automation)
- `nature-citation` — CNS citation export (for importing pipeline discoveries into manuscripts)
- `zotero` — library management (for long-term organization of pipeline outputs)
- `arxiv` — arXiv API (used as a search source)

## References

| Reference | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `references/scoring-system.md` | Six-dimension scoring rubric with weights, caps, and evaluation logic |
| `references/gap-analysis.md` | Methodology for identifying research gaps through systematic literature survey |
| `references/note-template.md` | Standardized literature note format with YAML frontmatter |
| `references/push-format.md` | Daily digest message template with field guidelines and example |
| `references/cron-setup.md` | Cron job creation, verification, and manual fallback procedures |
| `references/review-compilation-workflow.md` | End-to-end workflow for concentrated literature review writing |

## Pitfalls

1. **Keyword drift**: Review keywords monthly — research directions evolve
2. **Score inflation**: Subagents may inflate scores; always validate arithmetic
3. **Duplicate creep**: Classic papers will reappear; maintain a dedup index
4. **Wiki safety**: Pipeline writes to `raw/` only; wiki integration is manual
5. **Cron locality**: Hermes cron is local, not cloud — machine must be running

# Skill: nature-literature-pipeline

# Nature Literature Pipeline

A complete, production-tested automated literature pipeline. Not just "search for papers" — it's a structured engine that scores, classifies, reads, delivers, and archives research papers daily.

## What It Does

```
Cron (daily trigger, e.g. 08:30)
  │
  ├─ ① SEARCH (30 candidates)
  │   arXiv / OpenAlex / Crossref / Semantic Scholar (auto-degradation)
  │
  ├─ ② COARSE FILTER (30 → 5)
  │   Six-dimension scoring: topic match × 35 + methodology × 20
  │   + journal quality × 15 + network relevance × 10
  │   + applied value × 10 + archival value × 10
  │
  ├─ ③ FINE READ (top 5)
  │   Abstract-level or full-text. Source level tagged:
  │   Full-text / Abstract only / Metadata only
  │
  ├─ ④ DELIVER
  │   Formatted digest to Feishu/Telegram/etc.
  │   🏅 rank | title | journal | ⭐ score | 💡 one-liner
  │   🔬 methods | 📊 key results | 🧭 commentary
  │
  └─ ⑤ ARCHIVE
      DOI/arXiv de-dup → classify → write notes → update index
```

## Quick Start

After installing, tell your agent:

```
My research area is [X], keywords: [Y], deliver to [feishu group name], archive to [path]
```

The agent will configure keywords, delivery target, and archive path automatically.

Then set up a daily cron job:

```
Set up a daily literature push at 08:30 Beijing time, 30 candidates, top 5 delivered
```

## Architecture

The skill is organized in two layers:

| Layer | Purpose | Files |
|-------|---------|-------|
| **Engine** | Scoring, classification, note templates, gap analysis | `references/scoring-system.md`, `references/gap-analysis.md`, `references/note-template.md` |
| **Application** | Daily cron pipeline, delivery formatting, archival workflow | `references/push-format.md`, `references/cron-setup.md`, `references/review-compilation-workflow.md` |

## Configuration

All domain-specific content is configurable:

- **Keywords** — your research keywords (English + Chinese)
- **Scoring weights** — adjust the six dimensions for your field
- **Classification rules** — define your own tier system (A-E or custom)
- **Delivery target** — Feishu group, Telegram channel, email, etc.
- **Archive path** — local vault/wiki directory

A config template is provided in `templates/literature-push-template.md`.

## Built-in Safeguards

- **Score validation**: Each dimension capped, total recalculated — no 11/10 allowed
- **Triple de-duplication**: DOI / arXiv ID / OpenAlex ID
- **Graceful degradation**: Semantic Scholar down → auto-switch to OpenAlex + Crossref + arXiv
- **Read-only archive**: Daily pipeline writes to `raw/` literature directory only; never modifies wiki/knowledge base without user approval

## Related Skills

- `nature-academic-search` — ad-hoc literature search (complementary; this skill adds structured daily automation)
- `nature-citation` — CNS citation export (for importing pipeline discoveries into manuscripts)
- `zotero` — library management (for long-term organization of pipeline outputs)
- `arxiv` — arXiv API (used as a search source)

| Reference | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `references/scoring-system.md` | Six-dimension scoring rubric with weights, caps, and evaluation logic |
| `references/gap-analysis.md` | Methodology for identifying research gaps through systematic literature survey |
| `references/note-template.md` | Standardized literature note format with YAML frontmatter |
| `references/push-format.md` | Daily digest message template with field guidelines and example |
| `references/cron-setup.md` | Cron job creation, verification, and manual fallback procedures |
| `references/review-compilation-workflow.md` | End-to-end workflow for concentrated literature review writing |

## Pitfalls

1. **Keyword drift**: Review keywords monthly — research directions evolve
2. **Score inflation**: Subagents may inflate scores; always validate arithmetic
3. **Duplicate creep**: Classic papers

+# Literature scan: hyperbolic operations at discrete SID selection
+
+## Scope and constraints
+
+The target is to place a genuinely non-trivial hyperbolic operation in the decision that selects a discrete SID code, while preserving the frozen protocol: 32-dimensional latent vectors; exactly three 256-entry codebooks and exactly three integer SID tokens; original dataset, splits, Stage2 recipe, and Stage3 recipe. Any eventual candidate must strictly exceed all three reported gates: Hard-L1 ER > 16.38953942232631, Stage3 Recall@10 > 0.06406796775709883, and NDCG@10 > 0.03530651701940677. The literature below is not evidence that any such candidate will do so.
+
+The six already-closed families supplied in the task are excluded from the candidate list. This is a targeted prior-art scan, not an exhaustive novelty or patentability search.
+
+## Verified prior art
+
+| Identifier | Title | Year | Inspection level | Precise overlap |
+|---|---|---:|---|---|
+| DOI: [10.1609/aaai.v38i5.28261](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v38i5.28261); arXiv: [2401.07212](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.07212) | **HiHPQ: Hierarchical Hyperbolic Product Quantization for Unsupervised Image Retrieval** | 2024 | **ABSTRACT_ONLY** | Directly overlaps hyperbolic product quantization and image retrieval. The abstract identifies a hyperbolic product quantizer, hyperbolic codebook attention, and quantized contrastive learning on a hyperbolic product manifold. Thus hyperbolic structure is used in quantization/codebook construction, not only in an upstream embedding. It is unsupervised image retrieval, not recommendation. The inspected abstract does not establish the frozen 32-d / 3×256 / 3-token configuration, the given dataset or training recipes, nor any of the three required thresholds. |
+
+## Evidence boundary
+
+- The arXiv identifier, title, year, and abstract-level method description were checked against the arXiv record for 2401.07212. The DOI and AAAI 2024 venue association were cross-checked against the AAAI DOI record / publication metadata.
+- The full paper was not inspected in this pass. Accordingly, the entry is deliberately marked **ABSTRACT_ONLY**; no details about its exact assignment equation, numerical boundary conventions, or experimental compatibility are inferred.
+- Hyperbolic recommendation/ranking work that does not place a hyperbolic operation in discrete code selection is outside the requested overlap and is not presented as a match.
+- “Not identified” below means not found in this bounded scan, not proof of absence or a novelty opinion.
+
+## Candidate mechanism ideas not occupied by the inspected abstract
+
+These are research directions only, not validated mechanisms, and are stated to distinguish their decision operator from the abstract-level HiHPQ overlap. Each would need an explicit finite-precision contract (domain, epsilons, clamps, comparison tolerance, and boundary behavior) before implementation, and then a test under the frozen protocol.
+

+2. **Hyperbolic barycentric context-conditioned selection.** Form a context point by a declared hyperbolic barycenter of already-selected code-conditioned states, then choose the next code using a hyperbolic comparison against that context. The operation order must be fixed; no associator term is used. The inspected abstract does not establish this ordered, prior-code-conditioned assignment mechanism.
+4. **Hyperbolic triangle-defect decision.** Choose a code using a signed, orientation-defined defect formed from three hyperbolic distances involving the query, a code prototype, and a fixed anchor, with degeneracies and ties specified numerically. This is not the parked unsigned tangent-space wedge area. The inspected abstract does not disclose this decision statistic.
+
+These ideas remain unoccupied only relative to the single abstract inspected here; they are not cleared against full texts or the broader literature. In particular, item 4 must not be treated as a revival of the parked wedge-area candidate without a fresh definition and independent review.

# Skill: nature-literature-pipeline

# Nature Literature Pipeline

A complete, production-tested automated literature pipeline. Not just "search for papers" — it's a structured engine that scores, classifies, reads, delivers, and archives research papers daily.

## What It Does

```
Cron (daily trigger, e.g. 08:30)
  │
  ├─ ① SEARCH (30 candidates)
  │   arXiv / OpenAlex / Crossref / Semantic Scholar (auto-degradation)
  │
  ├─ ② COARSE FILTER (30 → 5)
  │   Six-dimension scoring: topic match × 35 + methodology × 20
  │   + journal quality × 15 + network relevance × 10
  │   + applied value × 10 + archival value × 10
  │
  ├─ ③ FINE READ (top 5)
  │   Abstract-level or full-text. Source level tagged:
  │   Full-text / Abstract only / Metadata only
  │
  ├─ ④ DELIVER
  │   Formatted digest to Feishu/Telegram/etc.
  │   🏅 rank | title | journal | ⭐ score | 💡 one-liner
  │   🔬 methods | 📊 key results | 🧭 commentary
  │
  └─ ⑤ ARCHIVE
      DOI/arXiv de-dup → classify → write notes → update index
```

## Quick Start

After installing, tell your agent:

```
My research area is [X], keywords: [Y], deliver to [feishu group name], archive to [path]
```

The agent will configure keywords, delivery target, and archive path automatically.

Then set up a daily cron job:

```
Set up a daily literature push at 08:30 Beijing time, 30 candidates, top 5 delivered
```

## Architecture

The skill is organized in two layers:

| Layer | Purpose | Files |
|-------|---------|-------|
| **Engine** | Scoring, classification, note templates, gap analysis | `references/scoring-system.md`, `references/gap-analysis.md`, `references/note-template.md` |
| **Application** | Daily cron pipeline, delivery formatting, archival workflow | `references/push-format.md`, `references/cron-setup.md`, `references/review-compilation-workflow.md` |

## Configuration

All domain-specific content is configurable:

- **Keywords** — your research keywords (English + Chinese)
- **Scoring weights** — adjust the six dimensions for your field
- **Classification rules** — define your own tier system (A-E or custom)
- **Delivery target** — Feishu group, Telegram channel, email, etc.
- **Archive path** — local vault/wiki directory

A config template is provided in `templates/literature-push-template.md`.

## Built-in Safeguards

- **Score validation**: Each dimension capped, total recalculated — no 11/10 allowed
- **Triple de-duplication**: DOI / arXiv ID / OpenAlex ID
- **Graceful degradation**: Semantic Scholar down → auto-switch to OpenAlex + Crossref + arXiv
- **Read-only archive**: Daily pipeline writes to `raw/` literature directory only; never modifies wiki/knowledge base without user approval

## Related Skills

- `nature-academic-search` — ad-hoc literature search (complementary; this skill adds structured daily automation)
- `nature-citation` — CNS citation export (for importing pipeline discoveries into manuscripts)
- `zotero` — library management (for long-term organization of pipeline outputs)
- `arxiv` — arXiv API (used as a search source)

## References

| Reference | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `references/scoring-system.md` | Six-dimension scoring rubric with weights, caps, and evaluation logic |
| `references/gap-analysis.md` | Methodology for identifying research gaps through systematic literature survey |
| `references/note-template.md` | Standardized literature note format with YAML frontmatter |
| `references/push-format.md` | Daily digest message template with field guidelines and example |
| `references/cron-setup.md` | Cron job creation, verification, and manual fallback procedures |
| `references/review-compilation-workflow.md` | End-to-end workflow for concentrated literature review writing |

## Pitfalls

1. **Keyword drift**: Review keywords monthly — research directions evolve
2. **Score inflation**: Subagents may inflate scores; always validate arithmetic
3. **Duplicate creep**: Classic papers will reappear; maintain a dedup index
4. **Wiki safety**: Pipeline writes to `raw/` only; wiki integration is manual
5. **Cron locality**: Hermes cron is local, not cloud — machine must be running
